abstract: Tropical forests contain remarkable phytochemical diversity, but the relationship between diverse plant metabolites and underlying climatic and environmental variation remains poorly understood. Mixture density networks (MDNs) offer a flexible approach for predicting variables with multimodal distributions. Traditional regression models produce single-value predictions, which may fail to capture the full variability of widely distributed variables. We evaluated the performance of an MDN model on a Panama metabolomics dataset, in which each metabolite occurs across multiple forest plots, resulting in environmental variables with multiple associated values. The MDN recovered the overall range and broad shape of environmental distributions, although feature-specific predictions often converged toward shared distributional patterns. These results suggest that mixture density networks can capture coarse environmental structure from metabolomic representations, while also highlighting challenges associated with limited environmental variation and sparse observations.
